title: The Graduate Collapse
briefing: Graduate recruitment at large professional-services firms has fallen 22% in two years. Employers say AI now does much junior research, drafting and analysis. Unemployment is stable and productivity is rising.

forecast.question: Chance graduate hiring in professional services is still 20% below its 2026 level in 2032.

briefingSignal.leansTrue: Assessment: firms are redesigning work around the absence of juniors, not pausing hiring. Analysts judge the fall is probably structural.
briefingSignal.leansFalse: Assessment: firms describe a hiring pause while they learn what the tools can do, and smaller employers are picking up graduates. Analysts judge the fall is probably transitional.

shah.stance: Two years of data from one sector. Publish better data and find out which kind of shock this is before spending billions.

harcourt.stance: Not my brief, but a generation with no route into professional work is a security problem in ten years.

chen.stance: Productivity is rising and unemployment is flat. A levy on firms for becoming more productive is a tax on the recovery.

okafor.stance: The bottom rung of the ladder has gone and it is not coming back. Build the replacement now, at scale.

choices.text: Let the market adjust and publish quarterly labour data.
choices.headline: Ministers decline to intervene in graduate hiring and commission quarterly labour data.
Large employers sign a compact on AI-augmented apprenticeships, backed by a government incentive.

choices.text: Levy on firms cutting junior intake, recycled into training.
choices.headline: A levy on firms that cut junior intake becomes law; proceeds go to training.
Government launches a national retraining programme for displaced graduates.

evidencePanel.known: US payroll data show a double-digit relative fall in employment for 22 to 25 year olds in AI-exposed jobs. A separate study found no discernible economy-wide disruption in the 33 months after ChatGPT's release.
evidencePanel.unknown: Whether junior roles are being eliminated or deferred. Most of the evidence is from the United States.
evidencePanel.whyItMatters: A structural shock rewards early, expensive action. A transitional one makes the same action look like waste.

sources.label: Stanford Digital Economy Lab, Canaries in the Coal Mine? (2025)
